title: Use of Topical JAK Inhibitors in Granulomatous Skin Diseases—A Retrospective Study
summary:
Non-infectious granulomatous skin diseases are rare inflammatory disorders characterized by the formation of granulomas, which are specific collections of immune cells within the skin. This group of diseases includes conditions such as granuloma annulare, necrobiosis lipoidica, and cutaneous manifestations of sarcoidosis. Available treatment options are often limited and do not always provide satisfactory results.

In recent years, so-called Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors have shown promising results in the treatment of several inflammatory skin diseases. Initial reports suggest that these medications may also be beneficial in granulomatous skin diseases.

In this study, the treatment outcomes of eight patients who received topical JAK inhibitors as part of individual treatment attempts at the Department of Dermatology, University Hospital Düsseldorf, will be retrospectively evaluated. The aim of the study is to assess the effectiveness of this treatment approach in chronic and difficult-to-treat granulomatous skin diseases.

For this purpose, patients will be categorized into two groups: those whose disease activity improved substantially during treatment (responders) and those who did not achieve sufficient improvement or had to discontinue treatment because of inadequate treatment response (non-responders).

The results of this study may help to better define the potential role of topical JAK inhibitors as a treatment option for these rare skin diseases.

interventions.name:
Between January 2024 and April 2026, a total of 8 patients with chronic, treatment-resistant granulomatous skin diseases were treated with topical JAK inhibitors as part of individual therapeutic trials at the Department of Dermatology at the University Hospital Düsseldorf.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Presence of a chronic, non-infectious granulomatous skin disease
- Treatment with a topical JAK inhibitor (ruxolitinib or delgocitinib)
- Treatment duration of at least 4 weeks
- Application twice daily, as discussed with the patient
Exclusion criteria:
- Evidence that the patients objected to the use of their data for research purposes at any point during the study.
- Treatment duration of less than 4 weeks or lack of compliance with the treatment regimen as documented in the medical history
